summary: The cross-user threats are covered by a negative criterion. The threat of a user writing a task's owner or id through the update body is rated high and has no criterion, and the plan applies the body's fields directly.

findings.title: T-3 has no criterion: the update can set a task's owner or id
findings.detail: Actor: a signed-in user. Action: PATCH their own task with ownerId or id in the body. Consequence: the task moves to another account or its id changes. The threat model names AC-4 as the verification, and the spec has no AC-4; plan step 2 applies the fields of the request body to the task.
findings.evidence: threat-model.md, Threats, T-3: rating high, verified by AC-4. spec.md has criteria AC-1 to AC-3 only. Plan step 2: 'Apply the fields of the request body to the task in the `PATCH` route'.
findings.requiredChange: Add a criterion that sends a field other than title and due in the update body and expects the request to be refused with nothing written, and make the plan parse the body field by field.
